content.introduction: Investing in healthcare stocks can provide stable returns due to the sector's resilience and consistent demand for medical services. The healthcare sector includes companies in pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, and medical devices. These stocks often offer dividends and can grow with advancements in medical technology.
body: * What is the health care sector? # Health care sector: Investing in stocks that help keep you well. Regardless of your age, condition, or financial situation, you likely spend some money on products and services to maintain your health, whether it’s a few bucks at the pharmacy or a major hospital visit. * Health care is prominent within the S&P 500; it’s one of the largest segments of the index’s 11 sectors. * Many health care industries are noncyclical, but some (like biotechnology) operate in emerging and speculative fields. Knowing which industries in the sector to invest in and when can help you position your portfolio for growth, mitigate market risk, and take advantage of both stable and speculative opportunities in the market. So if you’re thinking of adding health care stocks to your portfolio, get to know the industries and companies well, make sure they match your investment strategy, and pay attention to the regulatory and health-related trends affecting the sector.

Over 40% of adults in the U.S. and 16% globally are considered candidates for some form of weight loss support according to reports from the Center for Disease Control[2](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_ee96) and the World Health Organization,[3](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_8334) while heart disease remains the leading cause of death in the U.S.,[4](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_7c3) and cancer ranks second.[5](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_58b) Diabetes affects over 11% of the U.S. population,[6](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_f398) nearly half of U.S. adults have high blood pressure,[7](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_e1d) and mental health disorders affect millions of Americans annually,[8](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_e2c4) underscoring how many people rely on ongoing care and medication. McKinsey Company estimates that for every $10 billion in revenue, AI could help health insurers save between $150 million and $300 million in administrative costs, and up to $970 million in medical costs.[9](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_b64) Those potential savings help explain why many investors watch AI adoption closely, while also recognizing that healthcare organizations must implement changes carefully and within strict oversight. The healthcare sector is home to some of the most popular dividend stocks in our investment universe. The importance of healthcare in the lives of many consumers makes this sector one of the most stable and recession-resistant in the entire stock market, and allows well-managed healthcare companies to raise their dividends year in and year out. To that end, we’ve compiled a list of all 348 healthcare stocks (along with important investing metrics like price-to-earnings ratios and dividend yields) which you can download below:. The fundamental appeal of the healthcare sector makes an Excel database of all healthcare stocks very useful. The first filter will search for dividend-paying healthcare stocks with price-to-earnings ratios less than 20. **Step 2:** Click on the filter icon at the top of the price-to-earnings ratio column, as shown below. Moving on, the next example will show how to filter for dividend-paying healthcare stocks with dividend yields above 3% and market capitalizations above $10 billion.
